question: When may btrfs check --repair be run on a damaged filesystem?
statement: By default, btrfs check leaves the device unchanged; --readonly reaffirms that, while --repair attempts fixes. The documentation recommends unmounting before a check, though --force permits a mounted check. Use --repair only on a developer's or experienced user's advice and after accepting that no fsck can successfully repair every type of filesystem corruption. Finish or cancel any running replace or balance first. Without --force, repair displays a warning and waits ten seconds; --force allows mounted checks and skips mount checks and that warning delay. Mounted repair most likely causes corruption unless the filesystem is quiescent, which may not be possible to guarantee; an external device change can make a forced check crash.
quote: Do not use *--repair* unless you are advised to do so by a developer
